translations.idiomatic: The generals thought Northern Qi troops would surely not dare come out, and only sent scouts.

sentences.zh: 值連日陰霧，齊騎直前，圍洛之軍，一時潰散。

translations.literal: It happened that for days there was overcast fog; Qi cavalry came straight forward, and the army besieging Luoyang at once scattered.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that for days there was overcast fog; Northern Qi cavalry came straight forward, and the army besieging Luoyang at once scattered.

sentences.zh: 唯尉遲迥率數十騎扞敵，齊公憲又督邙山諸將拒之，乃得全軍而返。

translations.literal: It happened that for days there was overcast fog; Qi cavalry came straight forward, and the army besieging Luoyang at once scattered.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that for days there was overcast fog; Northern Qi cavalry came straight forward, and the army besieging Luoyang at once scattered.

sentences.zh: 權景宣攻克豫州，尋以洛陽圍解，亦引軍退。

translations.literal: It happened that for days there was overcast fog; Qi cavalry came straight forward, and the army besieging Luoyang at once scattered.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that for days there was overcast fog; Northern Qi cavalry came straight forward, and the army besieging Luoyang at once scattered.

sentences.zh: 楊摽於軹關戰沒。

translations.literal: Only Yuchi Jiong led several dozen horsemen to fend off the enemy; Duke of Qi Xian also directed the Mount Mang generals to resist them, and only then was the whole army able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuchi Jiong led several dozen horsemen to fend off the enemy; Yuwen Xian, Duke of Qi, also directed the Mount Mang generals to resist them, and only then was the whole army able to return.

sentences.zh: 護於是班師。

translations.literal: Quan Jingxuan captured Yu Province; soon, because the Luoyang siege was lifted, he too withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingxuan captured Yu Province; soon, because the Luoyang siege was lifted, he too withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 以無功，與諸將稽首請罪，帝弗之責也。

translations.literal: Yang Biao fell in battle at Zhi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao fell in battle at Zhi Pass.

sentences.zh: 護性甚寬和，然暗於大體。

translations.literal: Hu thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu thereupon withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 自恃建立之功，久當權軸。

translations.literal: For lack of merit, together with the generals he bowed and asked punishment; the Emperor did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: For lack of merit, together with the generals he bowed and asked punishment; the emperor did not blame him.

sentences.zh: 凡所委任，皆非其人。

translations.literal: Hu's nature was very mild and harmonious, yet he was dim regarding the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's nature was very mild and harmonious, yet he was dim regarding the larger pattern.

sentences.zh: 兼諸子貪殘，僚屬縱逸，恃護威勢，莫不蠹政害民。

translations.literal: Relying on his merit in establishment, he long held the pivot of power.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his merit in establishment, he long held the pivot of power.

sentences.zh: 上下相蒙，曾無疑慮。

translations.literal: All whom he entrusted were not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: All whom he entrusted were not the right men.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其暴慢，密與衛王直圖之。

translations.literal: Moreover his sons were greedy and cruel, his staff unrestrained; relying on Hu's authority, none failed to corrupt government and harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his sons were greedy and cruel, his staff unrestrained; relying on Yuwen Hu's authority, none failed to corrupt government and harm the people.

sentences.zh: 七年三月十八日，護自同州還。

translations.literal: Above and below deceived one another, and there was never doubt or concern.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below deceived one another, and there was never doubt or concern.

sentences.zh: 帝御文安殿，見護訖，引護入含仁殿朝皇太后。

translations.literal: High Ancestor, because of his arrogance and insolence, secretly plotted with Prince of Wei Zhi against him.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, because of his arrogance and insolence, secretly plotted with Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi against him.

sentences.zh: 先是帝於禁中見護，常行家人之禮。

translations.literal: Seventh year, third month, eighteenth day, Hu returned from Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, third month, eighteenth day, Yuwen Hu returned from Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 護謁太后，太后必賜之坐，帝立侍焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor attended at Wen'an Hall; when he had seen Hu, he led Hu into Hanren Hall to attend upon the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended at Wen'an Hall; when he had seen Yuwen Hu, he led Hu into Hanren Hall to attend upon the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 至是護將入，帝謂之曰：「太后春秋旣尊，頗好飲酒。

translations.literal: Before this, when the Emperor saw Hu within the forbidden precinct, he always observed family rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, when the emperor saw Yuwen Hu within the forbidden precinct, he always observed family rites.

sentences.zh: 不親朝謁，或廢引進。

translations.literal: When Hu attended upon the Empress Dowager, the Empress Dowager always granted him a seat, and the Emperor stood in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu attended upon the Empress Dowager, she always granted him a seat, and the emperor stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 喜怒之間，時有乖爽。

translations.literal: At this, as Hu was about to enter, the Emperor said to him: "The Empress Dowager's years are already advanced, and she greatly loves wine.
translations.idiomatic: At this, as Yuwen Hu was about to enter, the emperor said to him: "The Empress Dowager's years are already advanced, and she greatly loves wine.

sentences.zh: 比雖犯顏屢諫，未蒙垂納。

translations.literal: She does not attend court audiences, and sometimes omits receiving visitors.
translations.idiomatic: She does not attend court audiences, and sometimes omits receiving visitors.

sentences.zh: 兄今旣朝拜，願更啟請。

translations.literal: Between joy and anger there are at times departures from propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Between joy and anger there are at times departures from propriety.

sentences.zh: 」因出懷中《酒誥》以授護曰：「以此諫太后。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the "Admonition on Wine" from his bosom and gave it to Hu, saying: "Use this to remonstrate with the Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he took the "Admonition on Wine" from his bosom and gave it to Yuwen Hu, saying: "Use this to remonstrate with the Empress Dowager."

sentences.zh: 」護旣入，如帝所戒，讀示太后。

translations.literal: " Hu having entered, as the Emperor had instructed, read and showed it to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Hu having entered, as the emperor had instructed, read and showed it to the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 未訖，帝以玉珽自後擊之，護踣於地。

translations.literal: Before he finished, the Emperor struck him from behind with a jade tablet, and Hu fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the emperor struck him from behind with a jade tablet, and Yuwen Hu fell to the ground.

sentences.zh: 又令宦者何泉以御刀斫之。

translations.literal: He also ordered the eunuch He Quan to hack at him with the imperial blade.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the eunuch He Quan to hack at him with the imperial blade.

sentences.zh: 泉惶懼，斫不能傷。

translations.literal: Quan in fear and panic hacked but could not wound him.
translations.idiomatic: He Quan in fear and panic hacked but could not wound him.

sentences.zh: 時衛王直先匿於戶內，乃出斬之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Wei Zhi had first hidden inside the door, then came out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Wei Yuwen Zhi had first hidden inside the door, then came out and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 初，帝欲圖護，王軌、宇文神舉、宇文孝伯頗豫其謀。

translations.literal: At first, when the Emperor wished to plot against Hu, Wang Gui, Yuwen Shenju, and Yuwen Xiaobo had all taken part in the plan.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the emperor wished to plot against Yuwen Hu, Wang Gui, Yuwen Shenju, and Yuwen Xiaobo had all taken part in the plan.

sentences.zh: 是日，軌等並在外，更無知者。

translations.literal: That day, Gui and the others were all outside, and no one else knew.
translations.idiomatic: That day, Wang Gui and the others were all outside, and no one else knew.

sentences.zh: 殺護訖，乃召宮伯長孫覽等告之，卽令收護子柱國譚國公會、大將軍莒國公至、崇業公靜、正平公乾嘉，及乾基、乾光、乾蔚、乾祖、乾威等，並柱國侯伏侯龍恩、龍恩弟大將軍萬壽、大將軍劉勇、中外府司錄尹公正、袁傑、膳部下大夫李安等，於殿中殺之。

translations.literal: When Hu was killed, he then summoned the palace masters Zhangsun Lan and others and told them; at once he ordered the arrest of Hu's sons Pillar-of-State Yuwen Hui, Duke of Tan, Grand General Yuwen Zhi, Duke of Ju, Yuwen Jing, Duke of Chongye, Yuwen Qianjia, Duke of Zhengping, and Qianji, Qianguang, Qianwei, Qianzu, and Qianwei, together with Pillar-of-State Houfu Hou Longen, Longen's younger brother Grand General Wanshou, Grand General Liu Yong, Central and External Headquarters registrar Yin Gongzheng, Yuan Jie, Provision Department junior grandee Li An, and others, and killed them in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was killed, he then summoned the palace masters Zhangsun Lan and others and told them; at once he ordered the arrest of Hu's sons Pillar-of-State Yuwen Hui, Duke of Tan, Grand General Yuwen Zhi, Duke of Ju, Yuwen Jing, Duke of Chongye, Yuwen Qianjia, Duke of Zhengping, and Qianji, Qianguang, Qianwei, Qianzu, and Qianwei, together with Pillar-of-State Houfu Hou Longen, Longen's younger brother Grand General Wanshou, Grand General Liu Yong, Central and External Headquarters registrar Yin Gongzheng, Yuan Jie, Provision Department junior grandee Li An, and others, and killed them in the hall.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲白帝曰：「李安出自皂隸，所典唯庖廚而已。

translations.literal: Yuwen Xian, Duke of Qi, told the Emperor: "Li An came from the black-clad ranks; what he managed was only the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xian, Duke of Qi, told the emperor: "Li An came from the black-clad ranks; what he managed was only the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 旣不預時政，未足加戮。

translations.literal: Since he did not participate in current affairs, he does not merit execution.
translations.idiomatic: Since he did not participate in current affairs, he does not merit execution.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「公不知耳，世宗之崩，安所為也。

translations.literal: " High Ancestor said: "You do not know—Emperor Shizong's death was An's doing."
translations.idiomatic: " High Ancestor Yuwen Yong said: "You do not know—Emperor Shizong's death was Li An's doing."

sentences.zh: 」十九日，詔曰：

translations.literal: " Nineteenth day, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: " On the nineteenth day, an edict said:

sentences.zh: 君親無將，將而必誅。

translations.literal: Against ruler and parent there is no "will not"—if one does, execution is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Against ruler and parent there is no "will not"—if one does, execution is certain.

sentences.zh: 太師、大冢宰、晉公護，地寔宗親，義兼家國。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, chief minister, Duke of Jin Hu—by position he was truly imperial kin, in duty he embraced family and state.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor, chief minister, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu—by position he was truly imperial kin, in duty he embraced family and state.

sentences.zh: 爰初草創，同濟艱難，遂任總朝權，寄深國命。

translations.literal: At the first founding he together crossed hardship, then was entrusted with overall court power and deep charge of the state's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: At the first founding he together crossed hardship, then was entrusted with overall court power and deep charge of the state's mandate.

sentences.zh: 不能竭其誠效，罄以心力，盡事君之節，申送往之情。

translations.literal: He could not exhaust his sincere service, pour out his heart and strength, fulfill the minister's duty to the ruler, or express feeling in seeing off the departed.
translations.idiomatic: He could not exhaust his sincere service, pour out his heart and strength, fulfill the minister's duty to the ruler, or express feeling in seeing off the departed.

sentences.zh: 朕兄故略陽公，英風秀遠，神機穎悟，地居聖胤，禮歸當璧。

translations.literal: Our elder brother, the late Duke of Lueyang—heroic bearing lofty and far, divine wit sharp and keen, by position he stood among the sacred heirs, by ritual he was fit to receive the jade disk.
translations.idiomatic: Our elder brother, the late Duke of Lueyang—heroic bearing lofty and far, divine wit sharp and keen, by position he stood among the sacred heirs, by ritual he was fit to receive the jade disk.

sentences.zh: 遺訓在耳，忍害先加。

translations.literal: His final charge still in the ear—yet harm was first added against him.
translations.idiomatic: His final charge still in the ear—yet harm was first added against him.

sentences.zh: 永尋摧割，貫切骨髓。

translations.literal: Forever seeking the cutting wound, it pierces to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Forever seeking the cutting wound, it pierces to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 世宗明皇帝聰明神武，〔惟幾〕藏智。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong the Brilliant Emperor was intelligent, divine, and martial, [subtle in foresight] concealing wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong the Brilliant Emperor was intelligent, divine, and martial, subtle in foresight and concealing wisdom.

sentences.zh: 護內懷凶悖，外托尊崇。

translations.literal: Hu inwardly harbored fierce rebellion, outwardly relied on exalted honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu inwardly harbored fierce rebellion, outwardly relied on exalted honor.

sentences.zh: 凡厥臣民，誰亡怨憤。

translations.literal: Of all his ministers and people, who did not harbor resentment and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Of all his ministers and people, who did not harbor resentment and rage?

sentences.zh: 朕纂承洪基，十有三載，委政師輔，責成宰司。

translations.literal: We have inherited the great foundation for thirteen years, entrusting government to the master and tutor, charging the chief minister with completion.
translations.idiomatic: We have inherited the great foundation for thirteen years, entrusting government to the master and tutor, charging the chief minister with completion.

sentences.zh: 護志在無君，義違臣節。

translations.literal: Hu's intent was without a ruler; in duty he violated ministerial duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's intent was without a ruler; in duty he violated ministerial duty.

sentences.zh: 懷茲蠆毒，逞彼狼心，任情誅暴，肆行威福，朋黨相扇，賄貨公行，所好加羽毛，所惡生瘡痏。

translations.literal: Harbor this scorpion's poison, give rein to that wolf's heart; act on whim in execution and violence, freely wield authority and favor; faction stirs faction, bribes walk openly; what he favored gained feathers, what he hated sprouted sores.
translations.idiomatic: He harbored scorpion poison and gave rein to a wolf's heart; acted on whim in execution and violence, freely wielded authority and favor; faction stirred faction, bribes walked openly; what he favored gained feathers, what he hated sprouted sores.

sentences.zh: 朕約己菲躬，情存庶政。

translations.literal: We restrain ourselves and live plainly, keeping feeling for the hundred affairs.
translations.idiomatic: We restrain ourselves and live plainly, keeping feeling for the hundred affairs.

sentences.zh: 每思施寬惠下，輒抑而不行。

translations.literal: Whenever we think to extend grace and favor below, it is then suppressed and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever we think to extend grace and favor below, it is then suppressed and not carried out.

sentences.zh: 遂使戶口凋殘，征賦勞劇，家無日給，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Thus households and mouths wither, levies and corvée are exhausting; homes lack daily provision, the people cannot live.
translations.idiomatic: Thus households and mouths wither, levies and corvée are exhausting; homes lack daily provision, the people cannot live.

sentences.zh: 且三方未定，邊隅尚阻，疆埸待戎旗之備，武夫資扞城之力。

translations.literal: Moreover the three directions are not settled, the frontiers still blocked; the border awaits the banner of arms, fighting men rely on the strength to defend walls.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the three directions are not settled, the frontiers still blocked; the border awaits the banner of arms, fighting men rely on the strength to defend walls.

sentences.zh: 侯伏〔侯〕龍恩、萬壽、劉勇等，未效庸勳，先居上將，高門峻宇，甲第雕牆，寔繁有徒，同惡相濟。

translations.literal: Houfu [Hou] Longen, Wanshou, Liu Yong, and others had not achieved ordinary merit yet first held high command; lofty gates and towering eaves, armored mansions and carved walls—truly many were their kind, aiding one another in evil.
translations.idiomatic: Houfu Hou Longen, Wanshou, Liu Yong, and others had not achieved ordinary merit yet first held high command; lofty gates and towering eaves, armored mansions and carved walls—truly many were their kind, aiding one another in evil.

sentences.zh: 民不見德，唯利是視。

translations.literal: The people saw no virtue—only profit was regarded.
translations.idiomatic: The people saw no virtue—only profit was regarded.

sentences.zh: 百姓嗷嗷，道路以目；

translations.literal: The common people wailed, the roads passed in silence;
translations.idiomatic: The common people wailed, the roads passed in silence;

sentences.zh: 含生業業，相顧鉗口。

translations.literal: all living things trembled, looking at one another with mouths clamped shut.
translations.idiomatic: all living things trembled, looking at one another with mouths clamped shut.

sentences.zh: 常恐七百之基，忽焉顛墜，億兆之命，一旦阽危，上累祖宗之靈，下負蒼生之責。

translations.literal: Constantly we fear the foundation of seven hundred years may suddenly topple, the lives of billions may in one morning face peril; above we burden the spirits of the ancestors, below we fail the charge of the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Constantly we fear the foundation of seven hundred years may suddenly topple, the lives of billions may in one morning face peril; above we burden the spirits of the ancestors, below we fail the charge of the black-haired people.

sentences.zh: 今肅正典刑，護已卽罪，其餘凶黨，咸亦伏誅。

translations.literal: Now the canonical punishments are made upright; Hu has already received punishment, and the remaining evil faction have likewise submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Now the canonical punishments are made upright; Yuwen Hu has already received punishment, and the remaining evil faction have likewise submitted to execution.

sentences.zh: 氛霧旣清，遐邇同慶。

translations.literal: Mist and fog are already cleared; far and near alike rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Mist and fog are already cleared; far and near alike rejoice.

sentences.zh: 朝政惟新，兆民更始。

translations.literal: Court government is renewed alone; the myriad people begin anew.
translations.idiomatic: Court government is renewed alone; the myriad people begin anew.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下，改天和七年為建德元年。

translations.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed throughout the realm; change the seventh year of Tianhe to the first year of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty may be proclaimed throughout the realm; change the seventh year of Tianhe to the first year of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 護世子訓為蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Hu's heir Xun was made governor of Pu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's heir Xun was made governor of Pu Province.

sentences.zh: 其夜，遣柱國、越國公盛乘傳往蒲州，徵訓赴京師，至同州賜死。

translations.literal: That night, Pillar-of-State Yuwen Sheng, Duke of Yue, was sent by post relay to Pu Province to summon Xun to the capital; when he reached Tong Province he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: That night, Pillar-of-State Yuwen Sheng, Duke of Yue, was sent by post relay to Pu Province to summon Xun to the capital; when he reached Tong Province he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 護長史代郡叱羅協、司錄弘農馮遷及所親任者，皆除名。

translations.literal: Hu's chief administrator Chi Luoxie of Dai commandery, registrar Feng Qian of Hongnong, and those he personally favored and entrusted were all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's chief administrator Chi Luoxie of Dai commandery, registrar Feng Qian of Hongnong, and those he personally favored and entrusted were all struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 護子昌城公深使突厥，遣開府宇文德齎璽書就殺之。

translations.literal: Hu's son Yuwen Shen, Duke of Changcheng, was on mission to the Turks; an edict was sent with Palace Opener Yuwen De bearing the imperial seal to kill him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu's son Yuwen Shen, Duke of Changcheng, was on mission to the Turks; an edict was sent with Palace Opener Yuwen De bearing the imperial seal to kill him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔復護及諸子先封，諡護曰蕩，並改葬之。

translations.literal: Third year, an edict restored Hu and his sons' former enfeoffments, posthumously titled Hu Dang, and reburied them all.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, an edict restored Yuwen Hu and his sons' former enfeoffments, posthumously titled Hu Dang, and reburied them all.

sentences.zh: 叱羅協本名與高祖諱同，後改焉。

translations.literal: Chi Luoxie's original given name was the same as High Ancestor's taboo, and was later changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie's original given name was the same as High Ancestor Yuwen Yong's taboo, and was later changed.

sentences.zh: 少寒微，嘗為州小吏，以恭謹見知。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and humble; he once served as a minor clerk in the province and was known for respectful care.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was poor and humble; he once served as a minor clerk in the province and was known for respectful care.

sentences.zh: 恆州刺史楊鈞擢為從事。

translations.literal: Heng Province inspector Yang Jun promoted him to staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Province inspector Yang Jun promoted him to staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及魏末，六鎮搔擾，客于冀州。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei, the six garrisons were in turmoil, and he sojourned in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei, the six garrisons were in turmoil, and he sojourned in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 冀州為葛榮所圍，刺史以協為統軍，委以守禦。

translations.literal: Ji Province was besieged by Ge Rong; the inspector made Xie commander-in-chief and entrusted him with defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province was besieged by Ge Rong; the inspector made Chi Luoxie commander-in-chief and entrusted him with defense.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，協沒于榮。

translations.literal: Soon the city fell, and Xie was lost to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell, and Chi Luoxie was lost to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮敗，事汾州刺史爾朱兆，頗被親遇，補錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated, he served Fen Province inspector Erzhu Zhao and was much favored; he was appointed recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong was defeated, he served Fen Province inspector Erzhu Zhao and was much favored; he was appointed recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 兆為天柱大將軍，轉司馬。

translations.literal: When Zhao became pillar-of-heaven grand general, Xie was transferred to chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao became pillar-of-heaven grand general, Chi Luoxie was transferred to chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 兆與齊神武初戰不利，還上黨，令協在建州督軍糧。

translations.literal: When Zhao's first battle with Qi Shenwu went badly, he returned to Shangdang and ordered Xie to supervise army grain at Jian Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao's first battle with Gao Huan, Qi Shenwu, went badly, he returned to Shangdang and ordered Chi Luoxie to supervise army grain at Jian Province.

sentences.zh: 後使協至洛陽，與其諸叔計事，謀討齊神武。

translations.literal: Later he sent Xie to Luoyang to consult with his various uncles and plot to attack Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent Chi Luoxie to Luoyang to consult with his various uncles and plot to attack Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 兆等軍敗，還幷州，令協治肆州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhao and the others were defeated, they returned to Bing Province and ordered Xie to administer Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao and the others were defeated, they returned to Bing Province and ordered Chi Luoxie to administer Si Province.

sentences.zh: 兆死，遂事竇泰，泰甚禮之。

translations.literal: When Zhao died, he then served Dou Tai, and Tai treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao died, he then served Dou Tai, and Dou Tai treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 泰為御史中尉，以協為治書侍御史。

translations.literal: When Tai became censor-in-chief, he made Xie investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai became censor-in-chief, he made Chi Luoxie investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 泰向潼關，協為監軍。

translations.literal: When Tai marched toward Tong Pass, Xie was army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai marched toward Tong Pass, Chi Luoxie was army overseer.

sentences.zh: 泰死，協亦見獲。

translations.literal: When Tai became censor-in-chief, he made Xie investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai became censor-in-chief, he made Chi Luoxie investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其在關歲久，授大丞相府東合祭酒、撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫，轉錄事參軍，遷主簿，加通直散騎常侍，攝大行台郎中，累遷相府屬從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Tai marched toward Tong Pass, Xie was army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai marched toward Tong Pass, Chi Luoxie was army overseer.

sentences.zh: 協歷仕二京，詳練故事。

translations.literal: When Tai died, Xie was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai died, Chi Luoxie was also captured.

sentences.zh: 又深自克勵，太祖頗委任之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor, because he had been in Guan many years, appointed him eastern pavilion libationer of the grand chancellor's office, pacification army general, and silver-blue-golden-light grand master; transferred to recording secretary, promoted to chief clerk, added Regular Attendant through direct connection, acting grand mobile headquarters director, and successively promoted to staff officer of the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, because he had been in Guan many years, appointed him eastern pavilion libationer of the grand chancellor's office, pacification army general, and silver-blue-golden-light grand master; transferred to recording secretary, promoted to chief clerk, added Regular Attendant through direct connection, acting grand mobile headquarters director, and successively promoted to staff officer of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 然猶以其家屬在東，疑其有戀本之望。

translations.literal: Xie served through both capitals and was thoroughly versed in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie served through both capitals and was thoroughly versed in precedent.

sentences.zh: 及河橋戰不利，協隨軍而還。

translations.literal: Moreover he deeply restrained himself; Grand Progenitor greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he deeply restrained himself; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai greatly entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 太祖知協不貳，封冠軍縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Yet still, because his family remained in the east, he was suspected of longing for his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Yet still, because his family remained in the east, he was suspected of longing for his native place.

sentences.zh: 尋加車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the battle at He Bridge went badly, Xie returned with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the battle at He Bridge went badly, Chi Luoxie returned with the army.

sentences.zh: 九年，除直閤將軍、恆州大中正，加都督，進爵為伯，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor knew Xie was not double-minded and enfeoffed him as Baron of Champion county, fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai knew Chi Luoxie was not double-minded and enfeoffed him as Baron of Champion county, fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大都督、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was added chariots-and-cavalry general and left golden-light grand master.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was added chariots-and-cavalry general and left golden-light grand master.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖欲經略漢中，令協行南岐州刺史，幷節度東益州戎馬事。

translations.literal: Ninth year, he was made director of the palace guard, Heng Province chief impartial judge, added area commander, advanced to earl, fief increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year, he was made director of the palace guard, Heng Province chief impartial judge, added area commander, advanced to earl, fief increased by eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，卽授南岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to area commander and commissioner equal to Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to area commander and commissioner equal to Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時東益州刺史楊辟邪據州反。

translations.literal: At first Grand Progenitor wished to plan for Hanzhong and ordered Xie to act as governor of South Qi Province, together commanding the military horses of East Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: At first Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wished to plan for Hanzhong and ordered Chi Luoxie to act as governor of South Qi Province, together commanding the military horses of East Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 二年，協率所部兵討之，軍次涪水。

translations.literal: First year of Wei Emperor Fei, he was then appointed governor of South Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: First year of Western Wei Emperor Fei, he was then appointed governor of South Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 會有氐賊一千人斷道破橋。

translations.literal: At the time East Yi Province inspector Yang Bixie held the province and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time East Yi Province inspector Yang Bixie held the province and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 協遣儀同仇買等行前擊之，賊開路，協乃領所部漸進。

translations.literal: Second year, Xie led his troops to attack him; the army halted at Fu River.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, Chi Luoxie led his troops to attack him; the army halted at Fu River.

sentences.zh: 又有氐賊一千人邀協，協乃將兵四百人守硤道，與賊短兵接戰，賊乃退避。

translations.literal: It happened that Di bandits one thousand strong cut the road and broke the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Di bandits one thousand strong cut the road and broke the bridge.

sentences.zh: 辟邪棄城走，協追斬之，群氐皆伏。

translations.literal: Xie sent Commissioner Equal Qiu Mai and others forward to strike them; the bandits opened the road, and Xie then led his troops gradually forward.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie sent Commissioner Equal Qiu Mai and others forward to strike them; the bandits opened the road, and he then led his troops gradually forward.

sentences.zh: 以功授開府。

translations.literal: Again Di bandits one thousand strong intercepted Xie; Xie then led four hundred troops to hold the pass road and fought at close quarters; the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Again Di bandits one thousand strong intercepted Chi Luoxie; he then led four hundred troops to hold the pass road and fought at close quarters; the bandits then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仍為大將軍尉遲迥長史，率兵伐蜀。

translations.literal: Bixie abandoned the city and fled; Xie pursued and beheaded him, and the Di masses all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bixie abandoned the city and fled; Chi Luoxie pursued and beheaded him, and the Di masses all submitted.

sentences.zh: 旣入劍閣，迥令協行潼州事。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted palace opener.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was granted palace opener.

sentences.zh: 時有五城郡氐酋趙雄傑等扇動新、潼、始三州民反叛，聚結二萬餘人，在州南三里，隔涪水，據槐林山，置柵拒守。

translations.literal: He still served as chief administrator to Grand General Yuchi Jiong and led troops to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He still served as chief administrator to Grand General Yuchi Jiong and led troops to attack Shu.

sentences.zh: 梓潼郡民鄧朏、王令公等招誘鄉邑萬餘人，復在州東十裏，涪水北，置柵以應之。

translations.literal: Having entered Jian Pass, Jiong ordered Xie to administer Tong Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered Jian Pass, Yuchi Jiong ordered Chi Luoxie to administer Tong Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 同逼州城。

translations.literal: At the time Di chieftains of Wucheng commandery Zhao Xiongjie and others stirred the people of Xin, Tong, and Shi provinces to rebel; they gathered more than twenty thousand men three li south of the province, across Fu River, occupying Huailin Mountain, setting palisades and holding defense.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Di chieftains of Wucheng commandery Zhao Xiongjie and others stirred the people of Xin, Tong, and Shi provinces to rebel; they gathered more than twenty thousand men three li south of the province, across Fu River, occupying Huailin Mountain, setting palisades and holding defense.

sentences.zh: 城中糧少，軍人乏食。

translations.literal: Zitong commandery commoners Deng Fei, Wang Linggong, and others enticed townships of more than ten thousand men; again ten li east of the province, north of Fu River, they set palisades to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong commandery commoners Deng Fei, Wang Linggong, and others enticed townships of more than ten thousand men; again ten li east of the province, north of Fu River, they set palisades to respond.

sentences.zh: 協撫安內外，咸無異心。

translations.literal: Together they pressed the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Together they pressed the provincial city.

sentences.zh: 遣儀同伊婁訓、大都督司馬裔等將步騎千餘人，夜渡涪水擊雄傑，一戰破之。

translations.literal: Grain in the city was little, and the soldiers lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in the city was little, and the soldiers lacked food.

sentences.zh: 令公以雄傑敗，亦棄柵走還本郡。

translations.literal: Xie pacified within and without, and all were without divergent hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie pacified within and without, and all were without divergent hearts.

sentences.zh: 復與鄧朏等更率萬餘人，于郡東南隔水置柵，斷絕驛路。

translations.literal: He sent Commissioner Equal Yilou Xun, area commander Sima Yi, and others to lead more than one thousand infantry and cavalry, crossing Fu River by night to strike Xiongjie, and in one battle broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Commissioner Equal Yilou Xun, area commander Sima Yi, and others to lead more than one thousand infantry and cavalry, crossing Fu River by night to strike Zhao Xiongjie, and in one battle broke them.

sentences.zh: 協遣儀同楊長樂，與司馬裔等率師討之；

translations.literal: Linggong, because Xiongjie was defeated, also abandoned the palisade and fled back to his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Linggong, because Zhao Xiongjie was defeated, also abandoned the palisade and fled back to his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 復遣大都督裴孟嘗領百姓繼進，為其聲勢。

translations.literal: Again with Deng Fei and others he led more than ten thousand men, south of the commandery across water setting palisades, cutting off the post road.
translations.idiomatic: Again with Deng Fei and others he led more than ten thousand men, south of the commandery across water setting palisades, cutting off the post road.

sentences.zh: 孟嘗旣至梓潼，值水漲不得卽渡。

translations.literal: Xie sent Commissioner Equal Yang Changle, together with Sima Yi and others leading troops to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie sent Commissioner Equal Yang Changle, together with Sima Yi and others leading troops to attack them;

sentences.zh: 而王令公、鄧朏見孟嘗騎少，乃將三千餘人圍之數重。

translations.literal: again he sent area commander Pei Mengchang leading commoners to follow after, making a show of force for them.
translations.idiomatic: again he sent area commander Pei Mengchang leading commoners to follow after, making a show of force for them.

sentences.zh: 孟嘗以衆寡不敵，各棄馬短兵接戰。

translations.literal: When Mengchang reached Zitong, the water was high and he could not cross at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Mengchang reached Zitong, the water was high and he could not cross at once.

sentences.zh: 從辰至午，於陣斬令公及朏等。

translations.literal: Wang Linggong and Deng Fei, seeing Mengchang's horsemen were few, then led more than three thousand men and surrounded him several ranks deep.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Linggong and Deng Fei, seeing Pei Mengchang's horsemen were few, then led more than three thousand men and surrounded him several ranks deep.

sentences.zh: 賊徒旣失渠帥，遂卽散走。

translations.literal: Mengchang, because the many could not match the few, each abandoned his horse and fought at close quarters with short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mengchang, because the many could not match the few, each abandoned his horse and fought at close quarters with short weapons.

sentences.zh: 其徒黨仍據舊柵。

translations.literal: From chen to wu, on the field he beheaded Linggong and Fei and the others.
translations.idiomatic: From chen to wu, on the field he beheaded Wang Linggong and Deng Fei and the others.

sentences.zh: 而孟嘗方得渡水與長樂合。

translations.literal: The bandit followers having lost their chieftains, at once scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit followers having lost their chieftains, at once scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 卽勒兵攻柵，經三日，賊乃請降。

translations.literal: At once he led troops to attack the palisades; after three days the bandits requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At once he led troops to attack the palisades; after three days the bandits requested surrender.

sentences.zh: 此後數有反叛，協輒遣兵討平之。

translations.literal: After this there were several more rebellions; Xie always sent troops to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: After this there were several more rebellions; Chi Luoxie always sent troops to attack and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，太祖徵協入朝，論蜀中事，乃賜姓宇文氏，增邑通前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: Third year of Wei Emperor Gong, Grand Progenitor summoned Xie to court to discuss affairs in Shu, then granted the surname Yuwen and increased the fief together with the former to one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Third year of Western Wei Emperor Gong, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai summoned Chi Luoxie to court to discuss affairs in Shu, then granted the surname Yuwen and increased the fief together with the former to one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 晉公護旣殺孫恆、李植等，欲委腹心于司會柳慶、司憲令狐整等。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu having killed Sun Heng, Li Zhi, and others, wished to entrust his inner core to Director of Retainers Liu Qing and Director of Censors Linghu Zheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu having killed Sun Heng, Li Zhi, and others, wished to entrust his inner core to Director of Retainers Liu Qing and Director of Censors Linghu Zheng and others.

sentences.zh: 慶、整並辭不堪，俱薦協。

translations.literal: Qing and Zheng both declined as unable and together recommended Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing and Linghu Zheng both declined as unable and together recommended Chi Luoxie.

sentences.zh: 語在慶、整傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biographies of Qing and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the biographies of Liu Qing and Linghu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 護遂征協入朝。

translations.literal: Hu then summoned Xie to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu then summoned Chi Luoxie to court.

sentences.zh: 旣至，護引與同宿，深寄託之。

translations.literal: Having arrived, Hu received him to lodge together and deeply entrusted himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Having arrived, Yuwen Hu received him to lodge together and deeply entrusted himself to him.

sentences.zh: 協欣然承奉，誓以軀命自效。

translations.literal: Xie gladly accepted and served, vowing to give his life in service.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie gladly accepted and served, vowing to give his life in service.

sentences.zh: 護大悅，以為得協之晚。

translations.literal: Hu was greatly pleased and thought he had gained Xie too late.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu was greatly pleased and thought he had gained Chi Luoxie too late.

sentences.zh: 卽授軍司馬，委以兵事。

translations.literal: At once he was appointed army chief of staff and entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At once Chi Luoxie was appointed army chief of staff and entrusted with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋轉治御正，又授護府長史，進爵為公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to director of imperial governance, again appointed chief administrator of Hu's office, advanced to duke, fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to director of imperial governance, again appointed chief administrator of Yuwen Hu's office, advanced to duke, fief increased by one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 常在護側，陳說時事，多被納用。

translations.literal: Constantly at Hu's side, he set forth current affairs and much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Constantly at Yuwen Hu's side, he set forth current affairs and much was adopted.

sentences.zh: 世宗知其材識庸淺，每折之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong knew his talent and knowledge were shallow and mediocre, and always cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong knew his talent and knowledge were shallow and mediocre, and always cut him down.

sentences.zh: 數謂之曰：「汝何知也！

translations.literal: He often told him: "What do you know!"
translations.idiomatic: He often told him: "What do you know!"

sentences.zh: 」猶以護所親任，難卽屏黜，每含容之。

translations.literal: " Yet because Hu trusted and relied on him, it was difficult to dismiss him at once, and each time they made allowances for him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet because Yuwen Hu trusted and relied on him, it was hard to remove him at once, and each time they made allowances.

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，便授協司會中大夫、中外府長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Xie was promptly appointed Director of Audits grand master and chief secretary of the Palace and Exterior Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu died, Chi Luoxie was promptly appointed Director of Audits grand master and chief secretary of the Palace and Exterior Bureau.

sentences.zh: 協形貌瘦小，舉措褊急。

translations.literal: Xie was slight in build and small in stature; in bearing he was narrow and hasty.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Luoxie was slight in build and small in stature; in manner he was narrow and hasty.

sentences.zh: 旣以得志，每自矜高。

translations.literal: Once he had achieved his ambitions, he constantly vaunted himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had achieved his ambitions, he constantly vaunted himself.

sentences.zh: 朝士有來請事者，輒云「汝不解，吾今教汝」，及其所言，多乖事衷。

translations.literal: When court officials came to consult him on affairs, he would always say, "You do not understand—I will teach you now"—and what he said often missed the point of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials came to consult him, he would always say, "You do not understand—I will teach you now"—and what he said often missed the point.

sentences.zh: 當時莫不笑之。

translations.literal: At the time none failed to laugh at him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，追論平蜀功，別封一子縣侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, in rewarding merit for pacifying Shu, one of his sons was separately enfeoffed as marquis of a county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding (562), in rewarding merit for pacifying Shu, one of his sons was separately enfeoffed as marquis of a county.

sentences.zh: 又於蜀中食邑一千戶，入其租賦之半。

translations.literal: He was also granted an estate of a thousand households in Shu, with half its rents and taxes paid to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted an estate of a thousand households in Shu, with half its rents and taxes paid to him.

sentences.zh: 晉公護以協竭忠於己，每提獎之，頻考上中，賞以粟帛。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu, because Xie had served him wholeheartedly, constantly praised and rewarded him, repeatedly rated his performance as upper-middle, and rewarded him with grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, because Chi Luoxie had served him wholeheartedly, constantly praised and rewarded him, repeatedly rated his performance as upper-middle, and rewarded him with grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 遷少保，轉少傅，進位大將軍，爵南陽郡公，兼營作副監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to junior preceptor, then junior tutor; advanced to grand general; enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery; and concurrently appointed deputy supervisor of palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to junior preceptor, then junior tutor; advanced to grand general; enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery; and concurrently appointed deputy supervisor of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 宮室旣成，以功賜爵洛邑縣公，回授一子。

translations.literal: When the palaces were completed, for his merit he was granted the title Duke of Luoyi county and had it transferred to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When the palaces were completed, for his merit he was granted the title Duke of Luoyi county and had it transferred to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 協旣受護重委，冀得婚連帝室，乃求復舊姓叱羅氏。

translations.literal: Since Xie had received Hu's heavy commission, he hoped to marry into the imperial house and therefore asked to restore his former surname, the Chi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chi Luoxie had received Yuwen Hu's heavy commission, he hoped to marry into the imperial house and therefore asked to restore his former surname, the Chi clan.

sentences.zh: 護為奏請，高祖許之。

translations.literal: Hu memorialized the request; Gaozu approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu memorialized the request; High Ancestor Yuwen Yong approved it.

sentences.zh: 又進位柱國。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He was again advanced to pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 護以協年老，許其致仕，而協貪榮，未肯告退。

translations.literal: Hu, considering Xie was old, permitted him to retire from office, but Xie, greedy for glory, was unwilling to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, considering Chi Luoxie was old, permitted him to retire from office, but Chi Luoxie, greedy for glory, was unwilling to resign.

sentences.zh: 護誅，協除名。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Xie was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was executed, Chi Luoxie was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，高祖以協宿齒，授儀同三司，賜爵南陽郡公，時與論說舊事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, Gaozu, because Xie was advanced in years, appointed him grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and restored the title Duke of Nanyang Commandery; at the time he often discussed old affairs with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande (574), High Ancestor Yuwen Yong, because Chi Luoxie was advanced in years, appointed him grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and restored the title Duke of Nanyang Commandery; at the time he often discussed old affairs with him.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 子金嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jin succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 馮遷字羽化。

translations.literal: Feng Qian, styled Yuhua.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian, styled Yuhua.

sentences.zh: 父漳，州從事。

translations.literal: His father Zhang was a provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang was a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 及遷官達，追贈儀同三司、陝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Qian rose high in office, Zhang was posthumously granted grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and made governor of Shaan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Qian rose high in office, Zhang was posthumously granted grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and made governor of Shaan Province.

sentences.zh: 遷少修謹，有乾能，州辟從事。

translations.literal: Qian from youth was refined and cautious, possessed practical ability, and was recruited as a provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian from youth was refined and cautious, possessed practical ability, and was recruited as a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 魏神龜中，刺史楊鈞引為中兵參軍事，轉定襄令，尋為幷州水曹參軍。

translations.literal: During the Shengui era of Wei, Governor Yang Jun appointed him military aide, transferred him to magistrate of Dingsxiang, and soon made him water bureau aide of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era of Wei (518–520), Governor Yang Jun appointed him military aide, transferred him to magistrate of Dingsxiang, and soon made him water bureau aide of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 所歷之職，咸以勤恪著稱。

translations.literal: In every post he held he was known for diligence and conscientiousness.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he was known for diligence and conscientiousness.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，乃棄官，與直閤將軍馮靈豫入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Qian abandoned office and, with Direct-Palace General Feng Lingyu, entered Guan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Feng Qian abandoned office and, with Direct-Palace General Feng Lingyu, entered Guan.

sentences.zh: 卽從魏孝武復潼關，定回洛，除給事中。

translations.literal: He immediately followed Emperor Xiaowu in retaking Tong Pass and securing Huiluo, and was appointed gentleman-at-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately followed Emperor Xiaowu in retaking Tong Pass and securing Huiluo, and was appointed gentleman-at-attendance.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖擒竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Grand Progenitor in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shawei—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shawei—all with merit.

sentences.zh: 授都督、龍驤將軍、羽林監，封獨顯縣伯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander, Dragon-Prancing General, and superintendent of the Feathered Forest Guard; enfeoffed as Baron of Duxian county with an estate of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander, Dragon-Prancing General, and superintendent of the Feathered Forest Guard; enfeoffed as Baron of Duxian county with an estate of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽之戰，遷先登陷陣，遂中重瘡，僅得不死。

translations.literal: At the battle of Luoyang, Qian was first to scale the walls and break the line; he then received grave wounds and barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Luoyang, Feng Qian was first to scale the walls and break the line; he then received grave wounds and barely escaped death.

sentences.zh: 以功加輔國將軍、軍師都督，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to general who assists the state and military-affairs commander; his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to general who assists the state and military-affairs commander; his noble rank was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為廣漢郡守。

translations.literal: After a time he went out as governor of Guanghan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he went out as governor of Guanghan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時蜀土初平，人情擾動，遷政存簡恕，夷俗頗安之。

translations.literal: At the time Shu had just been pacified and popular sentiment was unsettled; Qian's government was simple and forbearing, and the barbarian customs were quite pacified thereby.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shu had just been pacified and popular sentiment was unsettled; Feng Qian's government was simple and forbearing, and the barbarian customs were quite pacified thereby.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，就加車騎將軍、大都督、通直散騎常侍，鎮樊城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was additionally made chariot-and-cavalry general, commander-in-chief, and regular attendant of the Direct-Liaison Secretariat; he garrisoned Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei (556), he was additionally made chariot-and-cavalry general, commander-in-chief, and regular attendant of the Direct-Liaison Secretariat; he garrisoned Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋拜漢東郡守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Handong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Handong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，入為晉公護府掾，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵臨高縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Qian entered service as an aide in Duke of Jin Hu's bureau; was promoted to chariot-and-cavalry grand general and grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies; and advanced in rank to Duke of Lingao county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin Yuwen Jue took the throne, Feng Qian entered service as an aide in Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu's bureau; was promoted to chariot-and-cavalry grand general and grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies; and advanced in rank to Duke of Lingao county.

sentences.zh: 尋遷護府司錄，進授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to director of records of Hu's bureau and was further appointed flying-cavalry grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and an open office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to director of records of Yuwen Hu's bureau and was further appointed flying-cavalry grand general and commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol and an open office.

sentences.zh: 遷性質直，小心畏慎，雖居樞要，不以勢位加人。

translations.literal: Qian by nature was upright; cautious and careful; though he held a pivotal post, he did not use rank and power to lord it over others.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian by nature was upright and cautious; though he held a pivotal post, he did not use rank and power to lord it over others.

sentences.zh: 兼明練時事，善於斷決。

translations.literal: He was also skilled and practiced in current affairs and good at deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled and practiced in current affairs and good at deciding cases.

sentences.zh: 每校閱文簿，孜孜不倦，從辰逮夕，未嘗休止。

translations.literal: Each time he examined documents he was tireless—from morning until evening he never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he examined documents he was tireless—from morning until evening he never ceased.

sentences.zh: 以此甚為護所委任。

translations.literal: For this reason Hu greatly relied on and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Yuwen Hu greatly relied on and entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 後以其朝之舊齒，欲以衣錦榮之，乃授陝州刺史，進爵隆山郡公，增邑幷前二千戶。

translations.literal: Later, because he was an elder of Hu's court, wishing to honor him with return in glory to his home region, Hu appointed him governor of Shaan Province, advanced his rank to Duke of Longshan Commandery, and increased his estate together with the former to two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he was an elder of Yuwen Hu's court, wishing to honor him with return in glory to his home region, Yuwen Hu appointed him governor of Shaan Province, advanced his rank to Duke of Longshan Commandery, and increased his estate together with the former to two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遷本寒微，不為時輩所重，一旦刺舉本州，唯以謙恭接待鄉邑，人無怨者。

translations.literal: Qian's origins were humble; the men of the age did not greatly esteem him—yet once he held provincial oversight over his native commandery, he received his home district only with humility and courtesy, and no one bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian's origins were humble and the men of the age did not greatly esteem him—yet once he held provincial oversight over his native commandery, he received his home district only with humility and courtesy, and no one bore resentment.

sentences.zh: 復入為司錄，轉工部中大夫，歷軍司馬，遷小司空。

translations.literal: He again entered service as director of records, transferred to grand master of the Ministry of Works, passed through military affairs secretary, and was transferred to minor minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He again entered service as director of records, transferred to grand master of the Ministry of Works, passed through military affairs secretary, and was transferred to minor minister of works.

sentences.zh: 自天和已後，遷以年老，委任稍衰。

translations.literal: From Tianhe onward, because Qian was old, his appointments gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: From Tianhe onward, because Feng Qian was old, his appointments gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，猶除名。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, he too was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was executed, he too was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 建德末，卒于家，時年七十八。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiande he died at home, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jiande he died at home, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 子恕，位至儀同三司、伏夷鎮將、平寇縣伯。

translations.literal: His son Shu reached the post of grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, general who garrisons Fuyi, and Baron of Pingkou county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu reached the post of grandmaster with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, general who garrisons Fuyi, and Baron of Pingkou county.

sentences.zh: 護所委信者，又有朔方邊平，位至大將軍、軍司馬、護府司馬。

translations.literal: Among those Hu relied on and trusted was also Bian Ping of Shuofang, who reached the posts of grand general, military affairs secretary, and military affairs secretary of Hu's bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Among those Yuwen Hu relied on and trusted was also Bian Ping of Shuofang, who reached the posts of grand general, military affairs secretary, and military affairs secretary of Yuwen Hu's bureau.

sentences.zh: 護敗，亦除名。

translations.literal: When Hu fell, he too was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu fell, he too was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：仲尼有言：「可與適道，未可與權。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Confucius said, "One may journey with someone on the Way, but one may not confer discretionary power on him.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Confucius said, "One may journey with someone on the Way, but one may not confer discretionary power on him.

sentences.zh: 」夫道者，率禮之謂也；

translations.literal: " The Way means adhering to ritual;
translations.idiomatic: " The Way means adhering to ritual;

sentences.zh: 權者，反經之謂也。

translations.literal: discretionary power means departing from the norm.
translations.idiomatic: discretionary power means departing from the norm.

sentences.zh: 率禮由乎正理，易以成佐世之功；

translations.literal: Adhering to ritual proceeds from correct principle and easily achieves the work of aiding the age;
translations.idiomatic: Adhering to ritual proceeds from correct principle and easily achieves the work of aiding the age;

sentences.zh: 反經系乎非常，難以定匡時之業。

translations.literal: departing from the norm depends on the extraordinary and is hard to settle the enterprise of righting the times.
translations.idiomatic: departing from the norm depends on the extraordinary and is hard to settle the enterprise of righting the times.

sentences.zh: 故得其人則治，伊尹放太甲，周旦相孺子是也；

translations.literal: Therefore when the right man is found there is order—Yi Yin deposed Tai Jia and the Duke of Zhou served the young lord are examples;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the right man is found there is order—Yi Yin deposed Tai Jia and the Duke of Zhou served the young lord are examples;

sentences.zh: 不得其人則亂，新都遷漢鼎，晉氏傾魏族是也。

translations.literal: when the wrong man is found there is chaos—the Xin capital moved the Han tripod and the Jin house overthrew the Wei clan are examples.
translations.idiomatic: when the wrong man is found there is chaos—Wang Mang moved the Han tripod and the Jin house overthrew the Wei clan are examples.

sentences.zh: 是以先王明上下之序，聖人重君臣之分。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings clarified the order of superior and inferior; the sages valued the distinction between ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former kings clarified the order of superior and inferior; the sages valued the distinction between ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 委質同於股肱，受爵均其休戚。

translations.literal: Entrusting oneself is like being hands and feet; receiving enfeoffment shares alike in weal and woe.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting oneself is like being hands and feet; receiving enfeoffment shares alike in weal and woe.

sentences.zh: 當其親受顧托，位居宰衡，雖復承利劍，臨沸鼎，不足以讋其慮；

translations.literal: When such a one personally receives a dying charge and stands in the place of chief minister, though he should take up a sharp sword or face a boiling cauldron, it is not enough to change his resolve;
translations.idiomatic: When such a one personally receives a dying charge and stands in the place of chief minister, though he should take up a sharp sword or face a boiling cauldron, it is not enough to change his resolve;

sentences.zh: 據帝圖，君海內，不足以回其心。

translations.literal: though he holds the imperial chart and rules all within the seas, it is not enough to turn his heart.
translations.idiomatic: though he holds the imperial chart and rules all within the seas, it is not enough to turn his heart.

sentences.zh: 若斯人者，固以功與山嶽爭其高，名與穹壤齊其久矣。

translations.literal: Men such as these—surely their merit contends with mountains and hills in height, and their fame with heaven and earth in endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as these—surely their merit contends with mountains and hills in height, and their fame with heaven and earth in endurance.

sentences.zh: 有周受命之始，宇文護寔預艱難。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Zhou received the mandate, Yuwen Hu truly shared in the hardships.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning when Zhou received the mandate, Yuwen Hu truly shared in the hardships.

sentences.zh: 及太祖崩殂，諸子沖幼，羣公懷等夷之志，天下有去就之心。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor died, the sons were young, the great lords harbored ambitions of equal standing, and the realm had minds inclined to depart.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai died, the sons were young, the great lords harbored ambitions of equal standing, and the realm had minds inclined to depart.

sentences.zh: 卒能變魏為周，俾危獲乂者，護之力也。

translations.literal: That he ultimately could transform Wei into Zhou and bring order out of peril was Hu's strength.
translations.idiomatic: That he ultimately could transform Wei into Zhou and bring order out of peril was Yuwen Hu's strength.

sentences.zh: 向使加之以禮讓，繼之以忠貞，桐宮有悔過之期，未央終天年之數，則前史所載，焉足以道哉。

translations.literal: If only he had added to this humility and deference and continued in loyalty and constancy—if the Palace of the Tung tree had had a term for repentance and Weiyang Palace a full span of years—then what the earlier histories record would be scarcely worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: If only he had added humility and deference and continued in loyalty and constancy—if the Palace of the Tung tree had had a term for repentance and Weiyang Palace a full span of years—then what the earlier histories record would be scarcely worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 然護寡於學術，昵近羣小，威福在己，征伐自出。

translations.literal: Yet Hu was poor in learning, drew close to petty men, kept favor and punishment in his own hands, and launched campaigns on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuwen Hu was poor in learning, drew close to petty men, kept favor and punishment in his own hands, and launched campaigns on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 有人臣無君之心，為人主不堪之事。

translations.literal: He had the heart of a minister without a lord and did what a sovereign cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: He had the heart of a minister without a lord and did what a sovereign cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 忠孝大節也，違之而不疑；

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety are the great norms—he violated them without hesitation;
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety are the great norms—he violated them without hesitation;

sentences.zh: 廢弒至逆也，行之而無悔。

translations.literal: deposing and murdering are the utmost rebellions—he practiced them without regret.
translations.idiomatic: deposing and murdering are the utmost rebellions—he practiced them without regret.

sentences.zh: 終於身首橫分，妻孥為戮，不亦宜乎。

translations.literal: In the end his body was cut in two at the neck and his wife and children slaughtered—is this not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: In the end his body was cut in two at the neck and his wife and children slaughtered—is this not fitting?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
